analysis:
This batch contains only documentation changes. The first is the new file changelog.d/ssd-restore-without-eval-lock.md (head lines 1-10). The second is docs/architecture/inference.md: a date bump at line 3, plus a new paragraph at head lines 252-259. That paragraph says the SSD complete-checkpoint import runs off the engine queue before engine.submit. It also says the import creates destinations directly from host bytes and never evaluates or fences them under MLX's process-wide evalLock. No source code is in this batch.

The security-relevant implication concerns T-041 (encrypted SSD prefix cache, TB-007, A-001). The described code change is in CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift, which is not supplied. Integration should verify that change against several properties:

(1) DBK3 AES-GCM authentication and the layout/weightHash/cacheSalt bindings still complete before the host bytes become engine-visible destinations. Skipping evaluation must not skip integrity checks.

(2) Creating MLX arrays from host bytes off the engine queue, without eval or fence, must not race with engine-thread state. This includes the staging reservation release paths (SSDPrefixCache.endAdoption/completeStaging and the EngineV2Bridge backstops named in T-041's detection_hint).

(3) Staging memory remains charged to the GlobalKVCacheBudget reservation; T-041 mitigation (e) depends on this.

(4) Timing: restore latency under contention drops from 2.6-3.8 s to about 0.35 s. This sharpens the hit/miss TTFT difference but stays within the accepted SEC-035 same-account oracle. The cross-account scope comes from the coordinator-authored cacheSalt, which this change does not alter. No threat-model update is evidently required by the docs alone.

The opt-in live test ModelCheckpointRestoreContentionLiveTests asserts timing only, not security.
